Hi David,

Thanks — we can provide everything requested. Quick summary here, and attached I will drop a compact pack with the CSV exports and remediation notes. Attachments: redwood_weekly_authenticated_scan_results_2027-10-08.csv, weekly-scan-cadence-configuration.csv, cve-2023-1456-closure-note.pdf, cve-2024-0098-remediation-summary.pdf

Key points:
- Cadence: Authenticated host and container scans run weekly for production and nightly for staging. Containers are scanned at build-time (CI) and again weekly in the registry.
- Scope: All customer-facing infra, control plane hosts, and internal build registries. We also include a sampled set of third-party base images (see note below).
- SLOs: Critical CVEs — remediation or compensating control in 30 days; High — 60 days; Medium/low — tracked and scheduled per sprint backlog with 90/180-day horizons. Exceptions require approval and are recorded in our remediation tracker.
- Evidence: CSV includes vulnerable artifacts, severity, first-seen, and remediation ticket link. The two CVE PDFs include remediation owner, timeline, and closure evidence (ticket IDs + PR links).

Regarding ownership of third-party images: primary ownership is the team that manages the service using the image; for base images we maintain a central third-party dependency log and flag critical findings for the infra team to action. Markus is copied for any handoffs.

I'll attach a signed VM attestation PDF in a follow-up email once our security lead signs it. If you need a different format (SPI/Excel), say the word.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Registry rescans: our weekly registry pipeline will automatically re-scan images for newly announced CVEs and also re-scan images when an upstream patch is released and we rebuild the image. For public base images we run weekly pulls of canonical tags we use and mark any changes; critical upstream advisories trigger immediate out-of-band rescans and notifications to the owning teams.
